Please design custom edge sensors and update the layout. Make a svg drawing showing:
- initial, non-realistic full coverage of ODD
- first 30ish coversge of nODD with |eta| < 4 coverage 
- optimized squares coverage
- optimized squares coverage with edge sensors

I’ll design edge sensor variants and compare all four layouts at the same endcap scale, with η contours on the SVG. I’ll treat |η| = 4 as the requested coverage target and check the aperture, packaging and support changes needed to reach it.

At the ECAL front (z = 3.95 m), |η| = 4 reaches r ≈ 145 mm, inside the current 300 mm aperture. Should the optimized layouts extend inward toward |η| = 4, or retain the aperture and show that region as uncovered?
- Extend optimized layouts toward |η| = 4 (prototype target)
- Keep the 300 mm aperture; show the |η| = 4 blind region

The current 300 mm aperture prevents front-face coverage to |η| = 4, even with edge sensors. I’ll make that limitation visible in the comparison. The Spack preflight also reports changed setup fingerprints, so I’m re-verifying DD4hep before running native geometry checks.

The optimized layouts will extend inward toward |η| = 4, as you confirmed. I’ll use broad quadrant carriers, compact square boards and custom boundary sensors with explicit passive guard regions. I’ll also define the edge pad shapes and readout mapping, rather than assigning full-size pads through the cut edges.

The first packing calculation gives **83.5% active face coverage with squares** and **88.1% with edge sensors**, using the same new aperture and service reservations. It adds 39 edge sensors per quadrant, with 22 distinct profiles before manufacturing review. I’m now checking the physical geometry, guard regions, pad mapping and native overlaps.

The geometry checks found no overlaps in either layout. The |η| = 4 scan also shows the remaining cracks: most sampled directions cross many active layers, but some support and board-gap directions receive fewer hits. The SVG will show the historical aperture limits and the new forward reach without implying uniform coverage.

The four-stage SVG is complete. It shows **98.6% for ODD’s idealized face, 31.9% for the original nODD plate, 83.5% for compact squares and 88.1% with edge sensors**, with the different historical denominators labelled. Both new layouts pass native overlap checks; I’m packaging the design catalogue, validation evidence and follow-up PR.

Validation is complete: both full ECAL endcaps have zero native overlaps, the pad mappings and boundary cases pass, and two Geant4 fixture events saved valid hits through a custom triangular sensor on both sides. I’m pushing the dedicated branch and opening the follow-up PR now.

[PR #70](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/70) is posted with the SVG and sensor catalogue, stacked on #69. Local checks pass and the token-site preview is green; I’m waiting for the final project CI check.

CI has reached the project-record and documentation checks. The delivered prototype preserves the old layouts for comparison and adds the new sensor masks, guards, readout mapping and endcap geometry on the dedicated branch.

Implemented and pushed as **[draft PR #70](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/70)**, stacked on #69.

|---|---:|

Historical layouts use their original faces; both optimized layouts share the same denominator.

The prototype adds rectangular, chamfered and triangular edge sensors, with explicit guards, electrodes and readout mapping. Both optimized layouts extend inward toward **|η| = 4**, as requested. At η = 4, **80% of sampled azimuths cross at least 40 of 48 active layers**; cracks remain.

Native geometry checks found **zero overlaps**, targeted Geant4 transport passed, and GitHub CI passed. Sensor fabrication and the smaller beam aperture remain engineering qualification tasks.
